w1.title: Worked Example 1: Proper, Improper & Mixed Fractions on the Number Line
w1.question: Plot 3/4 on a number line and find an equivalent fraction with denominator 12.

steps.text: Divide the interval from 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts; the 3rd mark is 3/4.
Verified equivalent fraction: 9/12 represents the exact same point.

check.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4 on the number line?

opts.m: Adding the same number to top and bottom changes the ratio.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form
w2.question: Reduce 18/24 to its simplest form.

steps.text: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 18 and 24, which is 6.
Divide both numerator and denominator by 6: (18 ÷ 6) / (24 ÷ 6).

check.q: What is the simplest form of 15/25?

opts.m: Do not invert the numerator and denominator.
Divide 15 by 5 to get 3 in the numerator.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Adding & Subtracting Fractions in Jal Seva Tank Audits
w3.question: A rainwater tank is 2/5 full in the morning and gains 3/10 more. What fraction is full now?

steps.text: Find the LCM of denominators 5 and 10, which is 10.
Convert 2/5 to 4/10 so both fractions have denominator 10.
Add numerators: 4/10 + 3/10 = 7/10 of the tank is full.

opts.m: Never add denominators directly; find the common denominator 6 first.
